Pairing · new wireless debugging on Android 11+

Code pairing is officially supported from Android 11 on phones and Android 13 on TVs. Availability depends on the target device firmware. On that device, open Developer options → Wireless debugging → Pair device with pairing code.
The pairing port and the connection port are different. Both are shown on the TV.

1. The device running this app must act as the USB host (OTG). Check that it supports OTG and enable it in settings if a switch is available. Connect an OTG adapter to this device if needed.
2. Use a working data cable: a charge-only cable will not work. Try another cable and connect without a hub or extension cable.

3. On the TV or box, use the port intended for connection to a computer (ADB/USB device). A regular USB port for flash drives may not support this role. Check the model’s manual for the correct port and cable.
4. Enable USB debugging in Developer options on the target device. Unlock the screens, allow this app to access USB, and accept the debugging prompt on the target device.
5. Reconnect the cable and tap “Refresh USB devices”. If that does not help, restart the devices. If no debugging prompt appears, revoke USB debugging authorizations on the target and reconnect.
If you cannot connect for USB debugging through the mobile app, try the desktop app for Windows, Linux, or macOS and connect the target device to your computer.
